names: Portions of Seawall Lot 349 and Pier 72
summary: The interim Prequel Park: about 2 acres per the Port memo (2.5 acres per the Power Station website, 2.75 per press), designed with Heatherwick Studio around Unit 3 and the 300-foot Stack, on the Power Station sub-area (which the 2018 Draft EIR describes as owned by the project sponsor) and on Port-owned shoreline land (portions of Seawall Lot 349 and Pier 72, leased to California Barrel Company for 66 years under Port Lease L-16662), of which about 0.4 acre is on Port property. The Port Commission amended the lease's permitted uses on Nov 18, 2025 (Resolution 25-70); the Port memo of Nov 2025 targets construction in 2026 and opening in 2027, and the project's BCDC amendment was issued June 26, 2026. No source found confirms construction has started.

details.text: Use of the interim park: the Port's Calendar Item 10A memo (November 14, 2025) lists multi-purpose lawn and sport courts, amphitheater seating, a quarter-mile walking and running track, water access, restrooms, interactivity with historic structures, art, food and beverage sales and kids' play; the San Francisco Chronicle (May 22, 2025) describes a 100-person amphitheater and a temporary art gallery in the Stack.

Scope of BCDC amendment 2019.006.02: the BCDC permit tracker's row for Non-Material Amendment 2019.006.02 (applicant California Barrel Company, LLC and Port of San Francisco; received 2025-06-19, issued 2026-06-26) describes 'in-kind interim park improvements and outdoor food and beverage area totaling approximately 57,000- 62,000 square feet until the underlying parcels may be developed for their final authorized uses'.
Address of the interim park: ICA SF's exhibition page for The Stack (undated) gives the address as '23rd & Maryland Streets'.

Hotel planned on the interim park site: SF Planning's project page (program elements, undated) gives 240,000 sq ft and 250 rooms; the San Francisco Chronicle (May 22, 2025) says 'The area around the stack ... is approved for the boutique hotel' and that its construction 'could be a decade away'.

Port lease uses: the Port's Calendar Item 10A memo (November 14, 2025) says the lease's permitted uses were amended by Resolution 25-70 (Nov 18, 2025) under lease Section 3.1 without a formal lease amendment.

Permanent shoreline program, full list from the Port's Calendar Item 10A memo (November 14, 2025): rip rap, Blue Greenway pathways and a potential boating dock; plazas, public art, gardens and picnic areas; informal play structures and site interpretation; a portion of the Bay Trail and a public recreational dock are the lease's permitted permanent uses.

open_questions: Corrected 2026-09-24: the timeline had shown 'under construction' today but 'planned' a couple of years in the future, because this record's map-shape status ('under construction') had not been updated to match its own sourced finding that no dated source confirms a construction start. The status was changed to 'planned', matching the related 'Prequel Park (Port sub-area)' record. Still true as of that correction: no dated source confirms construction has started; the latest primary statement is the Port memo (Nov 2025, start Q1 or Q3 2026) and ICA SF ('Construction begins in 2026', Oct 2025).

Whether the 2024 annual report's temporary activation east of Delaware Street and Stack Plaza ('Delaware East Park/Stack Plaza'; Andrea Cochran Landscape Architecture, schematic design from Aug 2024, construction then expected Q1 2026) is the same scheme later branded Prequel Park with Heatherwick Studio is not stated by any source.

Application filing: Chronicle (May 22, 2025) says the application was expected to be filed 'on Thursday'; SF YIMBY (Oct 2025) says 'In May, the developer submitted plans'. No Planning case number found.

Cost: the developer's own $15-20 million estimate (Chronicle, Potrero View) is the only figure for the whole park. DataSF building-permit applications for Prequel Park, all with status 'filed' and no issued date in the data read on 2026-10-12, list estimated costs of $4,000,000 (202512051053, block 9 landscape and exterior work, filed 2026-07-01), $1,500,000 (202512051066, Unit 3, filed 2026-07-01) and $1,500,000 (202512081182, admin building level 1, filed 2026-01-15): about $7.0 million for those three scopes. These are applicants' estimates for permit scopes, not contract values or the cost of the park; no construction contract was found.

BOS File 260724 (Amended and Restated DA; Board of Supervisors final passage Oct 6, 2026, enacted Oct 13, 2026 per Legistar's 'Enactment date') amends the Phasing Plan; whether it changes hotel or interim-park obligations is not stated in the legislative digest, and the draft DA text was not read.

Has Prequel Park construction started, and has the 2026 start been rescheduled? No dated source confirms that construction has started as of 2026-09-17 (searched sfport.com, sfplanning.org, Chronicle, SF YIMBY, Potrero View, SF Standard, developer site, ICA SF); as of 2026-10-10 no source read reports a groundbreaking or a new start date, and the developer's site still describes the park without reporting construction. DataSF's building-permit data read on 2026-10-12 shows the three Prequel Park applications (202512051053, 202512051066, 202512081182) as 'filed', with no issued date, and the BCDC permit tracker shows only the June 26, 2026 issuance of Non-Material Amendment 2019.006.02. The map status of this record is 'planned'.

BCDC amendment 2019.006.02: this record's mapping notes and timeline said it was 'issued June 19, 2025' (corrected 2026-09-29). The BCDC permit tracker gives June 19, 2025 as the date the application was RECEIVED and June 26, 2026 as the date ISSUED. The amendment document itself was not found on bcdc.ca.gov (2018-2019 DRB/Commission URLs now return 404; the tracker is an embedded table that could not be saved as text). Treat 2025-06-19 as application date, 2026-06-26 as issuance.

Port memo 10A is internally inconsistent: p.2 says construction start Q1 2026 / opening Q1 2027; p.4 says Q3 2026 / Q3 2027. Both are recorded; the p.4 dates follow the DBI-submittal sentence and are the more detailed statement.

The 'Spring 2026 SF development pipeline' listing ('Potrero Power Station - Prequel Park', developer FIFTH SPACE, scope demolition/grading/utilities/stormwater/landscaping) cited in this record's mapping notes could not be located online; no URL is on file.
Lease commencement date and the recorded lease are not in the corpus; 'March 2087' implies a ~March 2021 start but no source states it.
Exact footprint of the ~0.4 acre on Port land: memo Exhibit 1 is an unscaled rendering; not digitized.
Planning temporary use authorization (June 2025): no case number or document found on sfplanning.org.

Port Commission minutes of Nov 18, 2025: item 10A passed on consent with no discussion or public comment; the minutes URL is https://www.sfport.com/media/10953/download?inline (the meeting page's 'm11182025.pdf' link returns 'page not found').

No source read draws Prequel Park's boundary. The Port memo's Exhibit 1 is an unscaled schematic of the Power Station and Port sub-areas and the interim improvements, and the Power Station website's map page is an aerial rendering with no outline, so the shape on the map is Pier & Point's own composition.

Area of the whole interim park differs by source: about 2 acres (Port memo, Calendar Item 10A), 2.5 acres (developer site), 2.75 acres (Chronicle, ICA SF), 'almost three' (Potrero View); the BCDC amendment scope is 57,000-62,000 sq ft within the shoreline band only. The shape on the map is larger (about 3.4 acres) because it includes the ground of Blocks 4 and 9 and Humboldt Street Plaza, which the interim park is read to occupy until they are built. The developer-land share is not stated anywhere.

How long the interim park will run: the Port's Calendar Item 10A memo (November 14, 2025) says Thursday through Sunday 'for a period of at least five years beginning in 2027'; the San Francisco Chronicle (May 22, 2025) says it 'would likely last for five years'; the Potrero View (October 2025) says it would be 'replaced by a hotel sometime after 2032'. No source gives a closing date or says what replaces it on each parcel.

Historic structures in the park: the Potrero View (October 2025) describes Unit 3 as a former eight-story fossil gas-powered boiler; ICA SF's exhibition page (undated) plans a 'vertical gallery' in the Stack from fall 2027 (expected date). The San Francisco Chronicle (May 22, 2025) describes 'a skeleton-like structure that sits adjacent to the stack and used to hold a turbine' that 'will be filled with plants'; it does not name it Unit 3, and treating the two as the same structure is Pier & Point's reading.

Port land share of the park: the Port's Calendar Item 10A memo (November 14, 2025), p.3, says 'approximately .4 acres will be located on the Premises'; its Exhibit 1 splits that as about 0.15 acre for access to the future dock and about 0.25 acre for a multiuse lawn. The memo's text does not say who owns the rest of the roughly 2-acre park; Exhibit 1's ownership legend shows the interim improvements over the 'Power Station sub-area' and the 'Port sub-area', and the Draft EIR (October 2018) describes the Power Station sub-area as 'currently owned by the project sponsor'. Whether any of the park lies on other ownership is not stated.

Port parcel area: the Port's Item 13B memo (February 20, 2020) and the Draft EIR (October 2018) describe 2.9 Port-owned acres in three pieces: the largest, 1.6 acres, between the Power Station sub-area and the Bay (including water area for a potential recreational dock); 1.3 acres along 23rd Street; and a piece under a tenth of an acre ('Port Lands = 1.6 acres' on the memo's Exhibit 5, February 2020). The Port's Calendar Item 10A memo (November 14, 2025) says about 2 acres of the project's open space will be on Port-owned shoreline property (the lease Premises). No source says the Premises equal the 1.6-acre piece or where the Prequel Park footprint lies within it.

Sea level rise design: the Port's Calendar Item 10A memo (November 14, 2025) says the shoreline is elevated for projected sea level rise of 66 inches, adaptable if exceeded; the Port's Item 13B memo (February 20, 2020) gives 90 inches of sea level rise plus 42 inches of storm surge, 132 inches above current MHHW.

Public Trust Easement: under Resolution 20-12 the option covers approximately 1.97 acres of the developer's lands along the shoreline and in the 23rd Street right-of-way (the Port's Item 13B memo, February 20, 2020: 'approximately 1 acre of shoreline area and approximately 0.97 acres of roadway'). No source read shows the option was signed or recorded.
